pr_title: logind-dbus: set gc_mode to USER_GC_BY_PIN when disable linger
pr_body:
The mode switch from any to pin is currently done in create_session(). However, if no (pinning) session is created before (or after) linger is disabled, the user will not be gc'd after that. Therefore, also perform the mode switch when linger is being disabled.

Fixes #33488.

issue_context.title: user does not get terminated after linger is disabled
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

256.1

### Used distribution

Arch

### Linux kernel version used

6.9.6-arch1-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

loginctl, systemd-logind

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

user gets terminated after linger is disabled; `loginctl user-status $some_user` would give:
```
Failed to get user: User ID xxxx is not logged in or lingering
```

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

user does not get terminated after linger is disabled; the state is closing but it is never closed; `terminate-user` would stop the user manager and the slice, but apparently it's still not exactly "cleaned up".

note that if the user does not have linger enabled, and logged in on e.g. tty after a fresh (re)boot, logging out (i.e., stopping the last / only session left) will get the user terminated (and "cleaned up").

comments: Apparently it is a regression introduced in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/d2a4c37972494aaf3deea5bc971bc45ab8f73f25 (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/30884).

> the state is closing but it is never closed

I prepared #33651 for this.

review_comments: can you add a comment here, maybe something like: `/* Make sure that disabling lingering will terminate the user tracking if no sessions pin it. */`  or so?
